newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Rafsanjani to perform pilgrimage in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Rafsanjani to perform pilgrimage in Saudi.

text.p: Iran's outgoing President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani will visit Saudi Arabia this year and perform the minor Moslem pilgrimage of umra, a source close to the veteran Iranian leader said in remarks published on Monday.
"I have information that the visit of Mr Hashemi (Rafsanjani) to Saudi Arabia is long due," the source told Iran News daily.
Conditions for the visit were "quite favourable" and Rafsanjani would perform umra and meet Saudi leaders.
Relations between Tehran and Riyadh, two of the world's top three oil producers, have been tense since Shi'ite Moslem clergymen toppled the Iranian monarchy in 1979.
Diplomatic relations were severed from 1988 to 1991 after more than 400 people, mostly Iranians, died in riots during the annual pilgrimage to the holy city of Mecca in Saudi Arabia.

They were restored after the 1991 Gulf War, in which Iran remained neutral over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait, and have warmed further since the election in May of Rafsanjani's successor Mohammad Khatami.
Senior Gulf sources have said that the growing role of King Fahd's designated heir, Crown Prince Abdullah, in Saudi foreign affairs had led Riyadh to edge closer to Tehran.
Both men met on the sidelines of an Islamic summit in Pakistan in March and this had led to an invitation for Rafsanjani to visit the kingdom.
An envoy of the king made a rare visit to Iran this month.

Rafsanjani's visit will definitely occur before the December summit in Tehran of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference, a Saudi-based body which groups 52 Moslem countries, but not, evidently, before Rafsanjani leaves office early next month, the source told Iran News.
Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati on Sunday cast doubt on prospects for a visit, reflecting confusion during the run-up to Khatami's inauguration.
An official at Iran's diplomatic mission in the Saudi capital Riyadh said Rafsanjani was scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia later this year although the date was not yet clear.
But Velayati said: "I think Mr Rafsanjani's visit to Saudi Arabia is unlikely. If such a visit were due, the procedures should have been prepared by the Foreign Ministry."
Saudi-owned Asharq Al-Awsat newspaper on Sunday reported that Rafsanjani's visit would take place in November.
